title: Unbounded feasible region
back: $x+3y\ge3$, $x+y\ge2$: the region runs off to infinity. Smallest corner value of $Z=3x+5y$ is 7 at $B(\frac32,\frac12)$; the half-plane $3x+5y<7$ misses the region, so 7 is the minimum.

title: A whole edge of optimal points
back: $Z=3x+9y$ has the same value 180 at $C(15,15)$ and $D(0,20)$: every point of $CD$ gives the maximum. Minimum 60 at $B(5,5)$.

title: Objective function
back: The linear function to be maximised or minimised, subject to linear constraints and $x\ge0$, $y\ge0$.

title: Feasible region
tex: \text{common region of all constraints, with } x\ge0,\ y\ge0
back: Every point in it is a feasible solution. It is always convex. Bounded = can be enclosed in a circle.

title: Corner-point theorem
tex: \text{optimal value of } Z\ \Rightarrow\ \text{at a corner point}
back: If the region is bounded, both a maximum and a minimum exist, each at a corner.

title: Unbounded region: the extra check
tex: ax+by>M\ \text{ has no point in the region}\ \Rightarrow\ M\text{ is the maximum}
legend: M = largest corner value of Z
back: For a minimum $m$: check $ax+by<m$. If the half-plane does contain feasible points, there is no maximum (or minimum).

title: Same value at two corners
back: Then every point on the segment joining them is optimal: infinitely many solutions. Example: corners $(15,15)$ and $(0,20)$ give $q=3p$.

title: Reading a constraint from a graph
back: Write the line, then choose $\le$ or $\ge$ by testing a point inside the shaded region.

title: Which side to shade
back: True: shade the origin's side. False: the other side.
